text:
Aisha K.: Heads-up — I pushed a small prototype to show sampled per-invocation chargebacks in the console. 10% sampling by default, with a note about expected variance. please poke.
Ben (infra): Nice! Where's the branch? link?
Aisha K.: https://git.internal/r/redwood/cost-experiments/branch/sampled-invocation-ui
Aisha K.: key idea: store sample_weight on the telemetry row and extrapolate in the dashboard, rather than trying to retro-fit raw totals.
Chris M.: Be careful with bias — if routing changes correlate with the sample filter (eg. hotpath prefetched), extrapolation will mislead.
Dana: Agreed. We should attach routing metadata (route_id, model_sku, cache_hit) so we can stratify the estimator. otherwise variance explodes.
Sasha: For the Console UX, propose a toggle: "Show sampled estimate (x% sampling)" + hover explainer that shows CI. designers can mock a 95% CI band.
Ben (infra): Implementation note: we already emit sample_rate in the proto. Adding sample_weight is cheap. SQL to aggregate estimate:

```
SELECT
  route_id,
  SUM(cost * sample_weight) AS estimated_cost,
  COUNT(*) AS sampled_invocations
FROM invocation_events
WHERE sample_rate = 0.1
GROUP BY route_id;
```

Chris M.: That SQL assumes sample_weight = 1/sample_rate. fine, but if we do stratified sampling weights vary — need group-aware weights.
Aisha K.: Right — plan: sample_rate is stored per-row (float), sample_weight = 1.0/sample_rate. For stratified snapshot we keep sample_bucket tag too.
Dana: Also add a 'sample_id' (run id) so we can backfill later if sampling policy changes mid-window.
Sasha: UX question: do we show sampled numbers by default, or only as an advanced toggle? users will misunderstand unless it's explicit.
Aisha K.: My thought: default to exact counts for raw counters, but show "Estimated token cost" panels collapsed with a badge "sampled" and confidence when sampling < 100%.
Ben (infra): What about billing implications? We must never present sampled estimates as invoiceable. Add clear copy: "For internal visibility only — not final billing".
Chris M.: Edge case: canary routing will skew estimates if canaries have different token shapes. We should expose canary tag for drilldown.
Dana: +1. Also, preserve the pre-aggregation shape (distribution histograms) for sampled rows so variance is visible: mean, p50, p95 tokens.
Aisha K.: Good call. I'll add histogram aggregates to the prototype UI and wire sample metadata through the telemetry pipeline.
Sasha: For rollout, suggest feature-flag gated in Console (default off) and a spotlight for power-users. We'll add an inline tooltip: "Why is this different from invoice?"
Ben (infra): operational: need to ensure the ingestion pipeline propagates sample_weight to the cost materialized view; might need an extra column and re-partition.
deploy-bot: deploy started: cost-telemetry-proto update (sha: b3f4a0) — will roll canary to cluster-2
Chris M.: When can we run a quick sanity check? I'd like to compare sampled estimate vs full capture for a 1-hour window on a heavy route.
Aisha K.: I'll run a local replay job tomorrow and post results. goal: estimate error < 5% for routes > 1k invocations/hour at 10% sampling.
Dana: If error is larger, we can bump sampling on heavy routes dynamically (adaptive sampling). but that's a follow-up.
Sasha: UX acceptance criteria: (1) label "sampled" everywhere it appears, (2) show sample rate and CI on hover, (3) link to docs explaining estimator.
Aisha K.: Noted. I'll add a small docs blurb and a built-in "explain this number" modal.
Ben (infra): Thanks — +1 to the plan. ping me when you want the partition change scheduled.
Aisha K.: Thanks all :thumbsup: will post the replay output here tomorrow.
